summary: Documents the composition, selection, roles and organization of the Internet Architecture Board and its subsidiary organizations. It is informational. It was replaced by RFC 2850.

eli5.summary: A rulebook for the group that guides the Internet's design: who is on it, how they are chosen and what they do. A newer rulebook replaced it.

subtitle: How the Internet Architecture Board is composed, selected, and organized.

tldr.problem: The Internet's technical standards are developed through various groups, but there was no formal charter defining how the Internet Architecture Board (IAB) would be structured, how its members would be chosen, and what its responsibilities would be.
tldr.mechanism: The charter establishes the IAB as a 13-member body (the IETF chair plus 12 full members), sets selection procedures through a nominating committee, and defines its roles: approving the IESG leadership, providing architectural oversight, overseeing the standards process, managing the RFC series, external liaison, and advising the Internet Society.
tldr.outcome: The IAB charter provided governance structure for the Internet's technical leadership. It was later updated by RFC 2850 as the organization and Internet Society structures evolved, but established the foundational roles that continue today.

today: RFC 1601 is Informational and was obsoleted by RFC 2850. It established the IAB's formal governance structure, which continues to guide Internet standards development today. The IAB remains a key institution in the Internet's technical leadership, though the specific governance arrangements have been updated over time.

sections.title: The Internet Architecture Board and Its Role
sections.content:
The Internet Architecture Board (IAB) was chartered as a component of the Internet Society in June 1992 and serves as the technical leadership body for the Internet. Unlike an appointed committee of government officials, the IAB is composed of volunteers from industry, academia, and research institutions who serve individually, not as representatives of their employers. This structure allows the IAB to make decisions based on technical merit and the Internet's long-term health rather than organizational politics.

The charter documents the IAB's composition, how its members are selected, what roles and responsibilities it has, and how it is organized internally. It is an informational document that codifies practices the Internet community had adopted, providing transparency and continuity in the governance of Internet standards and architecture.
sections.eli5: The IAB is the group that decides the big questions about how the Internet works. This paper says who gets to be on the group and what they do.

sections.title: IAB Membership and Selection
sections.content:
The IAB consists of 13 voting members: the IETF chair (who also chairs the IESG) and 12 full members. Voting members serve two-year terms with no limit on the number of terms served. The IETF chair can vote on all IAB actions except approval of IESG members. The charter also allows for ex-officio members without voting rights, including the chair of the Internet Research Steering Group (IRSG) and the RFC Editor, who participate but cannot vote on official actions.

New voting members are nominated each year by an IETF nominating committee and approved by the Internet Society Board of Trustees (for the 12 full members) or by the 12 full IAB members (for the IETF chair). The nominating committee itself is formed annually with a non-voting chair designated by ISOC and seven members chosen at random from volunteers who have attended two IETF meetings in the prior two years. This random selection aims to prevent any group from dominating the process and keeps the selection process fair and transparent.
sections.eli5: The IAB has 13 voting members chosen each year. Anyone who goes to two IETF meetings can volunteer to help pick them. They serve two-year terms and can serve again.

sections.title: Primary Responsibilities and Functions
sections.content:
The IAB has six major responsibilities. First, it selects members of the Internet Engineering Steering Group (IESG), which directly oversees the standards development process. Second, it provides architectural oversight: reviewing proposed IETF working groups for consistency with Internet architecture and sponsoring the Internet Research Task Force (IRTF) for long-term research. Third, it oversees the standards process itself and serves as an appeal board for complaints about improper execution of that process.

Fourth, the IAB is responsible for editorial management and publication of the RFC series and designates the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA) to manage protocol numbers and other assignments. Fifth, it manages external relationships with standards bodies like ISO, IEC, ITU, and government organizations like the US Federal Networking Council. Finally, it advises the Internet Society Board on technical, architectural, and policy matters affecting the Internet. These roles collectively make the IAB responsible for the Internet's long-term technical direction.
sections.eli5: The IAB picks the leaders of the standards group, makes sure new standards make sense, publishes technical documents, and talks to other standards groups around the world.

sections.title: Internal Organization and Leadership
sections.content:
The IAB's chair is elected from among its full members to a one-year term with unlimited renewal. The chair has authority to organize the IAB and can be removed by a two-thirds vote of the IAB members. The chair appoints an Executive Director (ExecD) to handle internal administration: organizing meetings, managing conferences, and reporting results. The ExecD may be a voting IAB member or an ex-officio non-voting member.

The IAB chair also appoints or removes the chair of the Internet Research Steering Group (IRSG), who manages the IRTF. Additionally, the IAB chair and another IAB member serve as liaisons to the IESG, and the IESG appoints a liaison to the IAB. These liaison positions ensure communication between the two leadership bodies while maintaining their distinct roles.
sections.eli5: One IAB member is the chair and runs meetings. The chair can pick a helper (Executive Director) and picks who runs the research group.

sections.title: Standards Process Oversight and Appeal
sections.content:
The IESG directly develops and approves Internet Standards, but the standards process itself is established and documented by the IAB in consultation with the IESG and IETF. This means the IAB sets the rules for how standards are created, reviewed, and published, without micromanaging the IESG's day-to-day work. The IAB serves as an appeal board: if someone believes the standards process was executed improperly, they can bring their complaint to the IAB for review.

The IAB also conducts in-depth reviews of significant architectural issues. When needed, it convenes special panels of technical experts to examine particular areas, request presentations from affected IETF working groups, and issue reports with advice to the community. This allows the IAB to guide the Internet's evolution without dictating every technical detail.
sections.eli5: The IAB makes the rules for how standards are approved but lets the IESG do the actual work. If someone thinks the process was unfair, they can ask the IAB to review it.
